title: Requests to decompile binaries should be against TOS of GenAI tools
author: Frosty-Cockroach-807
selftext:
We're all aware that GenAI can be used to easily decompile and restructure code. This is a threat to game developers who risk their IP getting stolen with very little ability to prove it was stolen.

Yes decompiling was always a possibility before but it still required a set of skills and took much longer than simply prompting an AI agent. Even then you could still easily identify that the code was decompiled and stolen through a myriad of techniques (such as watermarking). But now the AI agent can just strip the resulting code of any watermarks etc.

These tools already reject requests that conflict with their existing terms of service (i.e. requests to assist with self-harm). It should not comply with adversarial requests used to steal and circumvent copyright law.
